Hi Sarah  thanks for the summary and the attachment. Well walk through the steps below and confirm next dates: 

1) Calculation window: Redwoods standard quarterly true-up runs on the 1st business week after quarter close. For Q2 this means we finalize numbers between Jul 5-7 (our finance calendar). The output is a reconciliation report (tokens committed vs actual) plus any make-good calculation.

2) Make-good mechanics: If youre under-committed, we issue a credit equivalent to the delta at the committed rate (per the signed amendment). Credits are applied to the next invoice cycle; in your case thats the July invoice unless you request an offset earlier.

3) Evidence: The Acme_Q2_Commit_Summary.xlsx is helpful. For robustness we also pull server-side per-model token logs from our billing pipeline; if you have a line-level export we can cross-check.

Im attaching a short operational checklist (see inline below) and will have Ben map the exact numbers so you have a single table to review.

Operational checklist (what happens after Jul 1):
- Jul 5: Redwood internal calc and cross-check with customer export.
- Jul 6: Draft reconciliation and make-good amount sent to customer.
- Jul 7: Customer confirmation window (48 business hours).
- Jul 12: Apply credit on next invoice (or earlier if both sides agree).

If that cadence works, Ben will follow up with the reconciliation snapshot and the underlying token math.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi all,

I ran a quick pass on Acmes spreadsheet and our billing export. A couple of notes on the math and rounding rules we apply so theres no surprise: 

- Token aggregation: We sum at the model variant level then roll up to the committed SKU. That prevents model-swap noise from inflating deltas.
- Rounding: We round down partial-token discounts at the SKU level for each invoice period; make-good credits use the committed per-token price multiplied by the integer token delta.
- Burst allowances: The amendment includes a 5% burst buffer per month. We treat burst as separate from commit; sustained overage beyond burst contributes to true-up delta.

Preliminary numbers (subject to final cross-check):
- Committed (H1 total): 1,200,000k tokens
- Actual (H1 usage projected from Q2 file + billing export): 1,144,600k tokens
- Delta: -55,400k tokens (under-commit)
- Credit at committed rate: $27,700 (applied as invoice credit unless you request a one-time refund)

Ill produce a reconciliation sheet with line-level model breakdown and upload it to the HubSpot deal record by Jul 5. If youd like us to fast-track the credit for an earlier invoice, say Jul 1, we can do so but will need the signed confirmation from Acme Ops by Jul 7.

Ben Carter
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
